pairs.subject: lazy-section-addressability
pairs.evidence: src/stores/navigationStore.ts:46 This shell moves between mutually exclusive module panes and tabs held in store state and URL query params, not between named positions on a long, lazily assembled scroll page; searches of src/app, src/hooks and src/stores for scrollIntoView, data-anchor, anchorId, hashchange and IntersectionObserver found nothing (location.hash only appears as a pass-through in useTabParam's replaceState, and sectionId only as a visibility-toggle key in useFeatureVisibility), so the subject's precondition does not hold.

techniques.evidence: src/app/page.tsx:27 The root page switches between whole shells; it does not compose an ordered list of scroll sections that would need unconditional address wrappers.

src/hooks/useTabParam.ts:6 The external address here is a query-param tab selector checked against validValues, not a hash anchor to an in-page section; there is no section-anchor namespace to split into two.

src/hooks/useScrollRestoration.ts:4 Scroll handling only restores a saved scrollTop per tab. No jump resolves a target inside a section that mounts as it nears the viewport, so no retry protocol is needed.
src/stores/navigationStore.ts:32 Locations are module and tab ids checked against the registry and tab-id lists, not DOM anchors whose live-page hosts could drift from a declared list.

pairs.registryProposal: navigationStore.ts:30-31 says a tab jump 'lands even when that module's pane mounts later', which is the address-vs-content split applied to tabbed app shells rather than long pages. The subject's precondition ('a long page') leaves out this neighbouring case; app-shell or session-resume might be a better home for it, or this subject could state the boundary explicitly.
